payload.title: drain-signals.js sweeps state file db-integrity-history.json → silent history wipe
payload.root_cause: drain-signals.js globs ALL docs/signals/*.json with NO state-file exclusion (line 33 readdirSync filter is *.json only). docs/signals/db-integrity-history.json is a PERSISTENT state array (read/written by scripts/db-integrity-history-append.sh, $HIST default path, HISTORY_CAP=200). On drain it is fingerprinted (from/to/type default to unknown/po/unknown), moved to docs/signals/processed/, then on the NEXT append run db-integrity-history-append.sh finds it missing, hits the catch branch and writes printf '[]' — silently destroying all history entries.
payload.evidence: Live drain tick 20260620T223928Z: had to relocate db-integrity-history.json out of the glob path to avoid the wipe; found an ORPHAN docs/signals/processed/db-integrity-history.json from a PRIOR mis-drain (untracked, never committed) = proof the trap already fired. Live file intact at 7 entries only because router excluded it manually this tick. An unattended/cloud drain would NOT exclude it.
fix_options: (a) drain-signals.js: skip files lacking a routable shape (no from AND no type), or apply an explicit state-file denylist (db-integrity-history.json + any non-signal *.json).

(b) PREFERRED: relocate the state file OUT of the drain inbox — move db-integrity-history.json to e.g. docs/data/db-integrity-history.json and update db-integrity-history-append.sh DB_INTEGRITY_HISTORY default + any reader. State files must not live in a drain inbox.
payload.verification_gate: Run node scripts/agents-flow/drain-signals.js with db-integrity-history.json present in docs/signals/ (or its new home) → file (and its entries) MUST survive the drain unchanged; processed/ MUST NOT receive a db-integrity-history.json copy.
payload.router_note: Router worked around this tick by relocate→drain→restore + removed the orphan processed/ copy. Definitif fix is dev-side per options above.
